title: Objects Together
goal: This lesson covers how several objects can work together in one program.
learn: Loop to call the same method on each
idea: Programs get interesting when objects work together. Make several players, put them in a list, and loop with for p in team: p.card(). It is the same class, many objects, and one loop. That is powerful and tidy.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change Mia's level to 5 and press Run. The last card should show Level 5.

practice.text: Make a list of two Dog objects and loop to print each name.
practice.hint: Inside the for loop, d is each Dog. Print d.name so Rex and Zoey show up on one line each.
practice.starterTip: Replace print() in the loop with print(d.name).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Rex and Zoey print via a loop over objects.

practice.text: Create three Players in a list. Loop and call a greet method you define.
practice.hint: Fill greet's print with self.name. Then team = should be a list of three Player(...) objects with different names.
practice.starterTip: team = [Player("Ava"), Player("Leo"), Player("Mia")] and in greet: print("Hi,", self.name).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if three greetings print from looped objects.

quiz.question: How can objects work together neatly?

options.text: Store them in a list and loop

quiz.correct: Right, lists of objects and loops scale well.
quiz.wrong: It looks like for p in team.

quiz.question: Do objects in a list need the same class?
quiz.correct: Yes, the same class makes looping over methods easy.
quiz.wrong: Think of a team of Players.

quiz.question: What does for p in team: p.card() do?

options.text: Calls card on each player object

quiz.correct: Right, you get one call per object.
quiz.wrong: It is a team roll call.

project.title: Team Roll Call
project.desc: Make a Player class with __init__ and a shout method. Put four players in a list and loop to shout for each one.
